subject.title: [Feature]: Automatically install brew if not installed

question: Should OpenClaw skill setup ever execute the Homebrew bootstrap installer when `brew` is missing, and under what consent/security policy?
rationale: The source path is clear, but automation should not decide whether onboarding may run external package-manager bootstrap code on the user's machine.

options.title: Keep Manual Guidance
options.body: Preserve the current policy: show Homebrew guidance, skip unavailable brew-backed installers, and avoid executing the Homebrew bootstrapper from skill setup.

options.title: Add Explicit Bootstrap
options.body: Allow an opt-in Homebrew bootstrap flow with maintainer-approved consent, provenance, timeout, logging, platform, and failure handling.

options.title: Limit Auto-Brew To Installer
options.body: Keep automatic Homebrew installation only in the top-level OpenClaw installer when needed for Node or Git, and leave skill dependencies manual.

recommendation.title: Keep Manual Guidance
recommendation.body: Preserve the current policy: show Homebrew guidance, skip unavailable brew-backed installers, and avoid executing the Homebrew bootstrapper from skill setup.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently owned the shared skill installer readiness path that would need to carry or reject this behavior.
